subject: Day 20: end of week 3; 1-month visit one week out
bodyText:
Today's focus
Day 20. Week three is closing. Head control is improving, movements are smoother and more symmetric, and recognition of parental voices is starting to show. The 1-month visit window opens in about a week.

Action items
- Confirm the 1-month well visit is booked within the day 28-35 window. AAP Bright Futures periodicity: https://www.aap.org/en/practice-management/bright-futures/bright-futures-tools-and-resources/
- Restock infant acetaminophen ahead of the 2-month vaccine visit; confirm the correct newborn dosing with the pediatrician. AAP HealthyChildren on fever and medication: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/health-issues/conditions/fever/Pages/default.aspx
- Continue daycare or nanny tours. ChildCare.gov directory: https://www.childcare.gov/
- Confirm Anoushka's 6-week postpartum visit is on the calendar. ACOG on the postpartum period: https://www.acog.org/womens-health/faqs/postpartum-pain-management
- Continue the feeding log.

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Smoother, more symmetric arm and leg movement; brief head lifts; cradle cap.
- [low concern] Blocked tear duct possible — continuous tearing in one eye without redness, resolves on its own.
- [monitor] Crying more than three hours a day on more than three days a week — the colic pattern, peaking at six to eight weeks.
- [call within 24h] Forceful projectile vomiting with weight loss. Persistent inability to console with back-arching during feeds.
- [call now] Rectal temperature at or above 100.4F (38.0C). Lethargy, refusing all feeds, blue or grey color, breathing faster than 60 per minute at rest, persistent grunting, projectile or bilious-green vomiting. Call 911 for blue lips or unresponsiveness!

Enrichment opportunities
- Keep tummy time at 15-20 minutes a day; lay him on your chest at an incline if he fatigues on the floor. AAP HealthyChildren on tummy time: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Back-to-Sleep-Tummy-to-Play.aspx
- Hold face-to-face conversations 8-12 inches away with slow, exaggerated speech.
- Take conversational turns with every coo and non-cry sound. Romeo et al., Psych Science 2018: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29442613/
- Read aloud daily; rhythmic, repetitive board books hold attention best.

Upcoming
- Day 28-35: 1-month well visit; first social smiles.
- Day 35-42: peak crying curve at about six weeks.
- Day 42: maternal 6-week postpartum visit.
